u1-s3-l1.alt: The handwritten Bill of Rights on old paper
u1-s3-l1.caption: The Bill of Rights, kept today at the National Archives in Washington, D.C.

u2-s1-l1.caption: The three branches. Each one has its own job, so no one branch has all the power.

u2-s2-l2.caption: Congress has two parts: the Senate (100 senators) and the House of Representatives (435 voting members).

u2-s2-l3.caption: Every state has 2 senators, so there are 100 in all.

u2-s2-l4.caption: How long each one serves: representatives 2 years, the President 4 years, senators 6 years.

u2-s2-l6.caption: Senators speak for their whole state: 2 from every state.

u2-s2-l7.caption: Representatives speak for one district. States with more people have more of them.

u2-s3-l3.caption: Each square is a state. The number is how many electors it has. States with more people have more electors.
There are 538 electors. To become President, a candidate needs 270 of their votes.

u2-s4-l3.caption: The Supreme Court has nine justices.

u4-s1-l1.alt: A portrait of a Navajo woman wearing a striped blanket, a silver necklace and a silver belt
u4-s1-l1.caption: A Navajo woman, about 1904. American Indians lived here long before the Europeans came.

u4-s1-l1.alt: A portrait of a Hopi man with long hair, wearing a blanket
u4-s1-l1.caption: A Hopi man. The Hopi are one of many American Indian tribes.

u4-s1-l1.alt: A painting of a man in dark clothes, said to be Christopher Columbus
u4-s1-l1.caption: Christopher Columbus was an explorer from Italy who sailed for Spain. He was European, not American Indian. He reached the Americas in 1492.

u4-s1-l2.alt: A map of eastern North America with the 13 colonies along the Atlantic coast
u4-s1-l2.caption: The 13 colonies were along the Atlantic coast.

u4-s2-l2.caption: Thomas Jefferson in 1800, the year before he became President.

u5-s1-l1.alt: A map of the United States in 1810. The Louisiana Purchase is a large green area in the middle, from the Mississippi River west to the Rocky Mountains
u5-s1-l1.caption: The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 is the large green area in the middle, between the Mississippi River and the Rocky Mountains.

u5-s3-l2.alt: An old photo of Susan B. Anthony
u5-s3-l2.caption: Susan B. Anthony led the fight for women’s right to vote.

u5-s3-l2.alt: An old photo of Harriet Tubman
u5-s3-l2.caption: Harriet Tubman escaped slavery and helped many others escape to freedom.

u6-s1-l2.alt: A black-and-white photo of a worried mother with her children
u6-s1-l2.caption: A mother and her children in 1936, during the Great Depression. Many families had no work and little food.

u6-s2-l1.caption: Franklin Roosevelt in 1933, the year he became President.

u6-s2-l2.alt: The official portrait of Dwight Eisenhower
u6-s2-l2.caption: Dwight Eisenhower, the 34th President.

u6-s4-l1.alt: A black-and-white photo of Martin Luther King, Jr.
u6-s4-l1.caption: Martin Luther King, Jr. in 1964.

u6-s4-l3.alt: A map of the Middle East showing Iraq, Kuwait and Afghanistan
u6-s4-l3.caption: A map of the Middle East. Kuwait is next to Iraq, and Afghanistan is farther east.

u6-s4-l4.alt: A black-and-white photo of the first airplane flying low over sand
u6-s4-l4.caption: The first airplane flight, by the Wright brothers, in 1903.

u6-s4-l4.alt: An astronaut standing on the moon
u6-s4-l4.caption: The first people landed on the moon in 1969.

u5-s2-l2.caption: The Union was in the North. The Confederacy was in the South. The war began at Fort Sumter, in South Carolina.

u5-s2-l3.alt: A black-and-white photo of Abraham Lincoln with a beard, in a dark suit
u5-s2-l3.caption: Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President, in 1863, the year of the Emancipation Proclamation.

u6-s1-l1.caption: The five wars of the 1900s that are on the test, in order.

u6-s3-l1.caption: In the Cold War, the United States and the Soviet Union were rivals with two different systems. It lasted from about 1947 to 1991.

u7-s1-l2.title: “The Star-Spangled Banner”
u7-s1-l2.caption: Listen to the national anthem, “The Star-Spangled Banner.”
